item.text: We prove that for every finite nonempty set \(A\) and every function \(f:A\to A\) satisfying condition \(C\), there exists \(a\in A\) such that \(f(a)=a\). The proof relies on both finiteness and condition \(C\). A supplied counterexample shows that the corresponding assertion for arbitrary infinite sets can fail even when \(C\) holds. This boundary limits the theorem’s scope and motivates asking which additional assumptions might support an infinite-set extension. It does not rule out existence results for more restricted infinite classes. We therefore formulate a conjecture for the restricted class \(K\): for every \(A\in K\) and every function \(f:A\to A\) satisfying \(C\), a fixed point exists under the additional compactness assumption \(D\). This proposed extension remains conjectural; no proof is supplied.
